claims.text: AuthController extends Notifier<String?>; build() returns null; signIn() only calls KeycloakSignIn.start(); completeSignIn and signOut assign state (the finished sign-in's token, null); authProvider is NotifierProvider<AuthController, String?>(AuthController.new).
A Notifier holds one value in state; its build() returns the initial value; a NotifierProvider creates the notifier and exposes its state; ref.read(provider.notifier) returns the notifier object.

claims.text: Only the notifier's methods change the value, by assigning state; when the new value differs from the old one (updateShouldNotify, == by default), every widget watching authProvider rebuilds.

claims.text: Notifier.state (getter and setter) is annotated @protected (and @visibleForTesting), so it is meant to be changed only inside the notifier; other code calls its methods.

WidgetRef.watch returns the value and rebuilds the widget when it changes; WidgetRef.read returns the value without listening. Riverpod's docs say watch belongs at the root of build, not in event handlers, and to consider read inside event handlers.
